10. In the instant case, petitioner Fateh Ram has testified the date as well as the manner of accident.
Despite cross- examination, no suggestion denying the occurrence of the accident or involvement of the offending vehicle has been put to PW-1.
Though suggestions qua petitioner not wearing a helmet or not holding a valid driving licence were put

Petitioner has sustained a rigorous cross-examination and nothing material to discredit him could be brought on record.
Further, after investigating even the police has filed a chargesheet against Respondent no.1 which shows that the accident was reported without any inordinate delay.
The site plan, mechanical inspection report and photographs of the offending vehicle are suggestive of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
11. In the present case, the driver or the owner of the offending vehicle have not filed their written statement.
Only suggestions denying rash & negligence of Respondent no.1 were put to PW-1 during cross-examination.
To rebut the claim of the petitioner they have not led any evidence in their defence.

It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd.

The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

As regards loss of income, petitioner has claimed to be working as a Beldar with Parliament Works Division-I, CPWD, Govt. of India at a salary of Rs.36,088/- per month.
Petitioner has proved his employment and salary by examining PW-2 Jitender Singh and by relying on his salary slip for month of September, 2017 as Ex.PW-1/3.
As per this salary slip, the net payable salary is shown to be Rs.23,442/-.

This salary record also shows that the petitioner did not draw any pay in the month of November, 2017 and December,

There is apparently no deduction in the salary in the month of October, 2017 i.e. the month in which the petitioner suffered the accident.

Also neither the salary slip Ex.PW-1/3 nor the salary record Ex.PW-2/A has been disputed by the insurance company while cross-examining PW-1 and PW-2.
Accordingly, salary of the petitioner is assumed to be Rs.23,442/- p.m. as on the date of accident.
It seems that there were deductions in his salary in October, 2017, perhaps on account of his leave owing to the accident.
Thus, the actual loss of income suffered by the petitioner on account of the accident is 2-1/2 months pay i.e. partially for October, 2017 and completely in November, 2017 and December,2017.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income equal to Rs.23,442/-X2.5=Rs.58,605/-.

Loss of future income/earnings:

In the present case, petitioner has relied upon disability certificate issued from Safdarjung hospital, noticing permanent disability of 80% PPI as per MRS Grading w.r.t. left upper and lower limb.
Petitioner has also claimed to have been rendered incapable of continuing his work post-accident.
He has pleaded that he has taken voluntarily retirement in 2019.
Petitioner has examined PW-2 and proved Ex.PW-2/A i.e. communication with regard to availing voluntary retirement.
No counter evidence has been led by the insurance company to show that the accident has no consequence on his working or was not a direct reason for his voluntarily retirement.
As per Aadhar card of the petitioner, his date of birth is 01.01.1960.

As per this document, date of his voluntary retirement i.e. 15.04.2019.
Petitioner would have been 59 years 3 months 10 days on the date of his voluntary retirement.
The future loss of income in this case would thus be 8 months and 20 days.

Accordingly, future loss of income (without applying multiplier or carrying out addition) would be his last drawn salary i.e.
Rs.26,337/-(as per salary detailed record Ex.PW-2/A).
Considering the age, nature of employment, retirement age,ed
, the functional disability of the petitioner is taken to be 20%.

As such, for purpose of calculating loss of future income, a multiplier of 9, as per Sarla Verma judgment, would be applicable in the case and 15% would be added as future prospect as Pranay Sethi judgment.
Hence, compensation towards loss of future income is assessed to Rs.26,337/-(monthly income)X9(approx. months)X9(multiplier)+15% of total income(as future prospect)=Rs.24,53,292/-.
20% of this amount would be Rs.4,90,658/-.
Hence so awarded.
